title: Customer wakeup-call triage notes - NovaHealth VPC latency spike
content:
Context and tl;dr:
- Night of 2027-03-21 -> 03:12 UTC NovaHealth (customer running private VPC on- prem) called wake-up pager: sudden tail latency for embedding API increased from ~45ms p50 to 400–650ms p99 for ~30 minutes.
- Impact: production embedding pipeline (batched requests via Dedicated gateway) had ~18% request timeout rate, downstream indexing backlog grew.
- This document captures the on-call triage, early hypotheses, temporary mitigations, handoff notes, and proposed follow-ups for the private-deployments team.

Attendees / responders (first 3 hours):
- Sofia Mendes (private-deploy on-call) – lead triage
- Ethan Park (SRE) – network diagnostics and BGP checks
- Maya Patel (Field install engineer) – customer network liaison, on-the-phone with NovaHealth NOC
- Lucas Nguyen (Serving runtime) – model-serving metrics and cache inspection
- Priya Rao (Customer success, NovaHealth POC) – customer comms

Timeline and key observations (ordered):
- 03:12 UTC pager fired (error rate surge detected by Redwood-Edge-monitoring; threshold: 5% 1-min error). alert DPL-4582 created.
- 03:14 UTC initial check: host-level cpu and GPU on private nodes normal; no OOM, no disk saturation.
- 03:20 UTC network traces from customer side show intermittent 30–50ms spikes between app nodes and storage (NFS) and occasional 200–400ms RTTs to the redis cache cluster.
- 03:25 UTC serving runtime logs show repeated retries and longer KV-cache fetch latencies (cache get p99 jumped from 8ms to 320ms).
- 03:30 UTC we observed an increased number of TCP retransmits on the customer edge router (counters incrementing).
- 03:40 UTC NovaHealth NOC reported a scheduled but staggered firewall rule push from their infra team that overlapped the incident window (they pushed new iptables rules to the border firewall at ~03:10 UTC).
- 03:48 UTC temporary mitigation applied: shifted embedding traffic to the regional fallback gateway (policy route), lowering request timeouts to ~2.4% in 10 minutes.
- 04:05 UTC confirmed queue drain on indexing pipeline but backlog remained ~12k items.
- 04:30 UTC handed off to day team with detailed notes; incident lingered as reduced performance until 06:00 UTC while customer reverted firewall rule push.

Early hypotheses (ranked):
1) Customer-side firewall rule push caused packet queuing and intermittent retransmits => increased TCP latency to backend caches and NFS (highest likelihood). Evidence: timing of firewall push, spike pattern, retransmit counters.
2) MTU mismatch on one of the transit paths causing fragmentation and performance cliffs for larger batched requests. Evidence: intermittent large RTTs and some ICMP 'fragmentation needed' records in traceroutes (low confidence).
3) Intermittent BGP route flap in customer's colo region causing short path changes and packet reorder (lower likelihood because BGP logs show no widespread flaps).
4) Application-level overload from unexpected burst (less likely; no CPU/GPU saturation, but redis latency spike remains central).

Diagnostics performed (commands / results shorthand):
- tcptraceroute and mtr run from customer app node -> redis nodes: spikes aligned with firewall push window, retransmits visible.
- netstat -s | grep retransmit -> tcp retransmits increased ~x350 over baseline.
- iptables-save diff (customer provided) showed new 'conntrack' heavy rule set added at 03:10 UTC with per-packet logging toggled.
- tcpdump (10s capture) showed bursts of delayed ACKs and duplicate segments; MSS tests suggested fragmentation for >1400 byte packets over one hop.
- serving runtime: cache hit path timing: /kv/get p99: 8ms -> 320ms; /nfs/read p99: 12ms -> 420ms.

Immediate mitigations applied (on-call changes):
- Route policy: temporarily shifted outbound requests to fallback regional gateway at 03:48 UTC (owner: Sofia) — reduced customer error rate quickly.
- Turned off batching bump (reduced typical request size) for NovaHealth's route to avoid fragmentation issues (owner: Lucas) — decreased p99 on KV fetch by ~60ms.
- Customer reverted firewall change at 05:56 UTC (NovaHealth confirmed), system metrics normalized by ~06:12 UTC.

Customer note (quote):
- "We pushed a firewall hardening change to close some legacy ports; it was rolled out staggered and we didn't catch the conntrack penalties. Sorry for the noisy night." — NovaHealth infra lead

Handoff summary to day team (what to chase):
- Verify no residual kernel conntrack memory pressure on customer's border firewalls. (Ethan / Maya – check with NovaHealth fw team; due 2027-03-23).
- Validate all private-deploy route fallbacks and rollback policies for late-night rollouts (SLA alignment and automation check). (Sofia / Lucas – due 2027-03-24).
- Add a temporary monitoring rule: flag conntrack transactions growth > x3 baseline for any customer (SRE) (Ethan – JIRA SRE-3910).
- Postmortem draft: collect full pcap, iptables diffs, and exact timestamps from NovaHealth for root-cause doc. (Priya / Sofia – draft due 2027-03-29).

Action items (owner — due):
- S1: Create postmortem skeleton and attach artifacts (Sofia Mendes — 2027-03-29).
- S2: Implement a per-customer conntrack/watchdog metric pipeline in Redwood telemetry (Ethan Park — 2027-04-07 — JIRA SRE-3910).
- S3: Add automated fallback trigger for suspected network-induced cache latency > 200ms p99 for 2 consecutive windows (Lucas Nguyen — 2027-03-31 — GH infrakit PR referenced).
- S4: Customer ops runbook update: include explicit checklist for firewall changes during business hours and a rollback plan (Maya Patel + Priya Rao — 2027-03-25).
- S5: Run a simulated night rollout with NovaHealth next week (table-top drill) to validate rollback and comms (Priya / Maya — 2027-03-30).

Notes to self / informal:
- We were lucky fallback gateway had capacity — must ensure we have headroom for similar events across multiple customers. Add capacity planning check to weekly cadence.
- Need to confirm whether conntrack logging was left enabled post-revert; excessive logging can also cause similar I/O pressure on firewalls.
- Consider adding a small experiment: reduce default batch size for private-deployments customers that opt into 'sensitive-network' profile. A/B test impact on per-token cost vs latency.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Did the firewall change interact with the customer's load-balancer health check cadence, causing additional retries?
- Exact MTU mismatch path — need tracert from each hop in colo and transit to be captured (ask NovaHealth for traceroutes 03:00–04:00 UTC).
- Should we expose a per-customer 'network posture' flag in the Console so install teams can tag customers who have aggressive firewall rules or constrained edge devices?

Attached artifacts (collected in incident folder):
- pcap_nova_030312-0312.pcap (provided by NovaHealth)
- iptables-diff-20270321.txt
- metric_screenshots/cache_latency_0300-0700.png
- incident-alert-DPL-4582.log

Next steps before postmortem:
- Gather missing artifacts from NovaHealth (pcap, traceroutes, firewall logs).
- Build timeline with exact second-level events and correlate with customer's change window.
- Draft RCA and share with the customer for factual confirmation prior to internal postmortem.

Status: in_review (postmortem skeleton exists; we need on-call + customer artifacts to finalize).

Notes for the weekly sync (private-deployments):
- Bring this case up on Friday triage to decide whether to classify as 'customer change/ops induced' vs 'platform resilience gap'. If classed as resilience gap, prioritize the automated fallback trigger work (S3) higher.
- Recommend 1-hour slot next week for runbook walkthrough with NovaHealth (Maya/Priya coordinate).

--end of notes--
